target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe deposits sourced from Wealth Management clients, held in U.S. subsidiaries/offices, and including sweep, savings, and time deposits. The 2025 disclosure (D051) confirms the source (Wealth Management clients), location (U.S. offices), and components (swept brokerage, time deposits) align with the 2024 definition.

The 2024 disclosures D151, D152, and D153 cover distinct aspects of the Deposits topic: D151 details time deposit composition (brokered CDs) and sweep balances; D152 covers source (Wealth Management), location (U.S.), and stability/cost characteristics; D153 covers cost profile differentiation and interest rate sensitivity. The 2025 disclosure D051 combines all these specific sub-topics into a single narrative, citing evidence for each: swept balances (ms_2025_7_P070_S001), brokered CDs (ms_2025_7_P071_S001), U.S. offices (ms_2025_7_P072_S001), Wealth Management/stability (ms_2025_7_P073_S001), and cost/profile sensitivity (ms_2025_7_P073_S002). Thus, D051 corresponds to the combined group.

comparisons.peer_summary: Deposits increased, reflecting an increase in CIB due to net inflows predominantly in Payments (largely offset by net maturities of structured notes in Markets), an increase in AWM due to growth in balances in new and existing client accounts reflecting higher-yielding product offerings (largely offset by migration into other investments), and a decline in CCB primarily driven by a decrease in balances in existing accounts due to increased customer spending and migration into higher-yielding investments (predominantly offset by new accounts).
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM describe an increase in total deposits for 2024, driven by growth in asset management/wealth segments and retail/client balances, partially offset by migration into other investments. MS reports an increase in total deposits due to Savings and Time deposits, offset by Brokerage sweep outflows to alternative products. JPM reports deposit increases driven by AWM (reflecting higher-yielding product offerings, offset by migration into other investments) and CIB, while CCB declined due to spending and migration. Both firms highlight the competitive dynamic of deposit growth being countered by client migration to alternative or higher-yielding investments.

sentences.text: Total deposits in 2024 increased primarily due to increases in Savings and Time deposits, partially offset by a reduction in Brokerage sweep deposits, largely due to net outflows to alternative cash equivalent and other investment products.

• an increase in AWM as a result of growth in balances in new and existing client accounts, reflecting the impact of higher-yielding product offerings, largely offset by continued migration into other investments, and

• a decline in CCB primarily driven by a decrease in balances in existing accounts due to increased customer spending and migration into higher-yielding investments, predominantly offset by new accounts.
